Helpers for code that drops the class

Source: R/vctrs.R
zu_ifelse.Rd

Base functions that build their result from the values without their class, such as ifelse() and vapply(), read a zuint vector's raw bits as numbers. These helpers do the same jobs and keep the type.

Usage

zu_ifelse(test, yes, no)

zu_vapply(X, FUN, FUN.VALUE, ...)

Arguments

test

A logical vector.

yes, no

Values for TRUE and FALSE, recycled to test.

X

A vector or list.

FUN

A function.

FUN.VALUE

A zuint or decimal128 vector of the length each result must have.

...

More arguments to FUN.

Value

A zuint vector.

Details

zu_ifelse() takes yes and no to their common type (see zu_common_type()) and is NA where test is. zu_vapply() calls FUN on each element of X and requires each result to have the length of FUN.VALUE, a zuint prototype such as int64(0); the results take its type. Both take decimal128() vectors too: zu_ifelse() combines yes and no as c() does, and zu_vapply() converts each result to the type of FUN.VALUE as x[i] <- value does, exactly or NA.

The same goes for sum(), min(), max(), range() and the other Summary functions, which R dispatches on their first argument only: sum(int128(5), 1L) is exact, while sum(1L, int128(5)) reads the raw bits. Put the zuint vector first.

base::matrix(), base::array(), base::outer() and base::diag() are such functions too, and no method can intercept them: they return the raw bits. zuint vectors do not form matrices, and the functions that dispatch refuse them with an error of class zuint_unsupported_error: %*%, base::crossprod() and base::tcrossprod() (the last two from R 4.4.0), cbind(), rbind(), as.matrix(), aperm() and scale().

Examples

x <- int64(c("-9223372036854775807", "5", NA))
zu_ifelse(x > 0L, x, int64(0))
#> <int64[3]>
#> [1]  0  5 NA
zu_vapply(1:3, function(i) uint64(2)^i, uint64(0))
#> <uint64[3]>
#> [1] 2 4 8
